findings_qualitative.value: Two redshifted high-velocity jets with bullet-like structures are identified: J1 oriented N-S from 4A1, and J2 oriented NE-SW (PA 29°) from 4A2.

evidence.quote: In the redshifted HV1 regime, a north-south jet (J1) stemming from source 4A1 is evident. The jet shows bullet-like structures and reaches almost ∼5′′ (∼1500 au) from the protostar.

We have successfully identified two distinct jets in the redshifted emission, originating from 4A1 and 4A2. The jet from 4A1 is oriented in a N-S direction, while that from 4A2, observed for the first time, exhibits a NE-SW orientation with a PA of 29◦ .

findings_qualitative.value: Four distinct outflows are identified in the IRAS 4A system (two driven by 4A1 and two driven by 4A2), and none of the outflow cavities is bent.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, we identify four distinct outflows in the region for the first time, with each protostar, 4A1 and 4A2, contributing to two of them.
Each protostar has two outflow systems, with 4A1 showcasing three outflow cavities and 4A2 presenting four. Contrary to prior studies, we argue that none of the outflows is bent.

findings_qualitative.value: The feature at 20–25'' north of 4A2 previously interpreted as a sharp bend or directional variability is instead the remnant of the western wall of a second, low-velocity outflow cavity (C4-red).

evidence.quote: However, we suggest that it is rather linked with the LV component of the 4A2 outflow (C4-red; see Sect. 3.3), being the remnant of its western cavity wall.

Our study challenges previous interpretations of the directional variability observed in the outflow of IRAS 4A2, suggesting instead that it represents the remnants of the western wall of the lowvelocity outflow cavity.

findings_qualitative.value: The misalignment of the cavities from each protostar and the lower velocities of the more extended cavities indicate episodic ejection events with jet precession in both 4A1 and 4A2.

evidence.quote: We propose that the misalignment of the cavities is due to a jet precession in each protostar, a notion supported by the observation that the more extended cavities of the same source exhibit lower velocities, indicating they may stem from older ejection events.

findings_qualitative.value: A velocity gradient of 3–7 km s−1 between the western and eastern walls of the C2-red cavity indicates possible cavity rotation.

claims.hypothesis: The complex northern emission and multiple southern lobes in the NGC 1333 IRAS 4A system arise from multiple distinct, unbent outflows driven by both 4A1 and 4A2 rather than bent outflows.
claims.experiment: Mapped and compared velocity-resolved channel maps and moment maps of SiO(5–4), H2CO(3(0,3)–2(0,3)), and HDCO(4(1,4)–3(1,3)) at ~150 au resolution from ALMA FAUST data.
claims.result: Identified two redshifted jets (J1 from 4A1 at PA 0° and J2 from 4A2 at PA 29°), two bow shocks (Bow1 at 10'' and Bow2 at 18''), three cavities from 4A1 (C1-red, C1-blue at PA 0°, extension 10''; C3-blue at PA -12°, extension 13''), and four cavities from 4A2 (C2-red/blue at PA 29°, extension 18''/13''; C4-red/blue at PA 26°, extension 25''/23'').
claims.finding: Four distinct outflows exist in the IRAS 4A system (two from each protostar), and none of the outflow cavities is bent.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, we identify four distinct outflows in the region for the first time, with each protostar, 4A1 and 4A2, contributing to two of them. We characterise the morphology and orientation of each outflow, challenging previous suggestions of bends in their trajectories.
Each protostar has two outflow systems, with 4A1 showcasing three outflow cavities and 4A2 presenting four. Contrary to prior studies, we argue that none of the outflows is bent.

claims.hypothesis: The arc-like structure at 20–25'' north-northeast of IRAS 4A2 previously attributed to a deflection/directional variability of the 4A2 jet by an external dense core is instead part of an older outflow cavity wall.
claims.experiment: Examined low- and intermediate-velocity H2CO and SiO channel maps alongside HDCO moment 0 emission to trace the eastern and western walls of the northern emission.
claims.result: Detected C4-w at 25'' and an eastern counterpart C4-e at 15'' in LV maps (8–12.5 km s−1) that together form an elliptical cavity (C4-red) with PA ~26° centred on 4A2.
claims.finding: The feature previously interpreted as directional variability is the western cavity wall of a second, low-velocity outflow cavity driven by 4A2.

evidence.quote: We propose that C4-w and C4-e together form an elliptical shape with a PA of ∼26◦, directed towards 4A2, implying they trace a second outflow system driven by 4A2 (C4-red), where C4-w represents the western wall and C4-e is the eastern.
Hence, the structure previously thought to be a sharp bend (directional variability; Choi 2005; Yıldız et al. 2012; De Simone et al. 2022) is actually part of the western cavity wall of C4-red.

claims.hypothesis: The misalignment between the two outflow systems of 4A1 (0° vs -12°) and of 4A2 (29° vs 26°) is caused by jet precession and episodic ejections in each protostar.
claims.experiment: Compared the extensions, position angles, and velocities of the multiple cavities per protostar, and checked literature astrometry across epochs for proper motion.
claims.result: More extended cavities exhibit lower velocities (e.g., C4-red at ~10 km s−1 vs C2-red at ~16 km s−1; C3-blue at ~15 km s−1 vs C1 at ~18 km s−1), and protostellar coordinates show no significant proper motion.
claims.finding: Each protostar experienced at least two episodic ejection events with precessing jets, and the more extended cavities represent older decelerated ejections.

evidence.quote: We propose that the misalignment of the cavities is due to a jet precession in each protostar, a notion supported by the observation that the more extended cavities of the same source exhibit lower velocities, indicating they may stem from older ejection events.

To verify that the misalignment is attributed to a precession rather than the potential shifting position of protostars over time, we examined the presence of proper motions of this source. We found no significant proper motion

why_this_data.value: Three shock/outflow tracers (SiO, H2CO, HDCO) observed at high spatial (~150 au) and spectral resolution in the ALMA FAUST Large Program provide complementary insights into jets, bow-shocks, and cavities of different ages/velocities.

evidence.quote: We employ these three tracers because a posteriori and after a fast check of the maps for this source we found that they offer complementary insights into the observed dynamics, with H 2 CO and HDCO playing a crucial role in identifying the cavities and enriching our understanding of the system’s dynamics.

why_this_method.value: Primary beam attenuation correction was omitted to preserve morphological features extending toward or beyond the edge of the field of view.

evidence.quote: By not applying correction for primary beam attenuation, we ensure that features extending beyond the field of view, are not inadvertently excluded in our analysis.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Bent northern outflow cavities from 4A1 and/or 4A2 (rejected based on the detection of Bow1 at 10'' closing the N-S 4A1 cavity and Bow2 closing C2-red)

evidence.quote: We contend that neither of the cavities is bent. In fact, the non-detection of the bow-shock Bow1 in the previous studies has led to uncertainties regarding the extent and orientation of the cavity associated with 4A1, where it was thought that it is extended up to ∼17′′ and bent to the east.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Deflection / directional variability of the 4A2 jet by an external dense core at ~20'' (rejected in favour of C4-w being the western wall of an older low-velocity outflow cavity C4-red)

evidence.quote: Initially, this structure was attributed to a deflection of the 4A2 outflow caused by a dense core (Choi 2005). However, we suggest that it is rather linked with the LV component of the 4A2 outflow (C4-red; see Sect. 3.3), being the remnant of its western cavity wall.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Proper motion of the protostars over time causing cavity misalignment (rejected after checking historical coordinates and finding no significant proper motion)

evidence.quote: To verify that the misalignment is attributed to a precession rather than the potential shifting position of protostars over time, we examined the presence of proper motions of this source. We found no significant proper motion

limitations_admitted.value: Narrow spectral window of SiO limits detection at velocities beyond 35 km s−1.

evidence.quote: The narrow spectral window limits detection beyond 35 km s−1, however, the emission is expected to be relatively low beyond this velocity threshold.

limitations_admitted.value: Extended emission of C4-red and the distant SiO blob at ~35'' from 4A2 are partially filtered out or lie outside the field of view.

evidence.quote: The cavity is not entirely detected, likely due to filtering.

evidence.quote: It is worth noting that the SiO blob at ∼35′′ from 4A2 observed by Choi (2005); De Simone et al. (2022) is ∼6′′ out of our FoV and was not detected in our observations due to filtering.

limitations_admitted.value: Spatial resolution (~150 au) is insufficient to resolve potential close binary companions (~12 au) for 4A1 and 4A2 to determine the physical cause of jet precession.

evidence.quote: With our observations, it is challenging to determine the origin of the precession of 4A1 and 4A2’ jets, as the identification of a potential binary companion for each protostar would require an angular resolution of about 12 au.
